note: Mined all 110 MP3s in C:/Users/foste/Desktop/music-ai with mutagen 1.48.1 (0 unreadable): 51 artists, 17-edge remix graph from 13 remixers covering all 8 the ask named, ratio 87 ORIGINAL / 16 cross-artist remix-class (14.5%), ID3 coverage TIT2/TPE1/TALB/APIC 110/110 with date/genre/TPE4 at 0/110, two mtime batches (2026-08-05 n=54 remix-first, 2026-10-01 n=56 originals-backfill) with the curation direction read filed; gaps stated in the receipt: no release years or genres exist in the tags so no era axis is derived from them, three classifier defects were caught and fixed in-lane, and no mag/ or tools/ code was touched so the ratchet was not run.

rows.claim: The spotdown.org tagger encodes remix credits only in the title suffix and the TPE1 comma pair; the ID3 remixer frame TPE4 is empty in all 110 files, so any remix-graph miner must parse both informal slots and use the TPE1-part-not-in-suffix rule to recover the original artist.
rows.steal: One seat, one sitting: before trusting any downloaded-corpus metadata pipeline, dump its frame inventory and write the parser against the frames that actually exist (here TIT2 suffix + TPE1 comma pair), not the frames the spec says should exist.
rows.falsifier: A spotdown-family corpus where TPE4 is populated, or a track whose TPE1 comma pair and title suffix disagree about who remixed whom, kills the two-slot law.

rows.claim: The folder's curation ran in two phases 57 days apart: the 2026-08-05 batch bought the remix network (18.5% remix-class share, every named 12-inch credit) and the 2026-10-01 batch backfilled original catalog depth around a fixed 13-artist core (remix share down to 10.7%).
rows.quote: BATCH 2026-08-05: 54 files, 33 unique artists, remix-class share (REMIX+VS+EDIT) 10/54 (18.5%)
rows.steal: One seat, one sitting: cluster any playlist-download folder by file mtime before computing folder-level stats, and file the per-batch delta, because the two batches answer different curation questions.
rows.falsifier: A multi-batch folder whose mtime clusters show no remix-share or artist-core delta between batches (differences within a few percent) kills the phase law.

rows.claim: The canon's measured shape is roughly 80% originals / 20% remix-adjacent with one hub artist on both sides of the edge (Justice: 12 tracks as artist plus 2 credits as remixer) and one busiest hand (Soulwax: 3 remixes plus 6 tracks); the style is the graph, not the track list.
rows.steal: One seat, one sitting: when a corpus claims a genre identity, compute the artist-side and remixer-side degree tables; a genre whose hub positions are empty (nobody appears on both sides) is a flat playlist, not a scene.
rows.falsifier: A french-touch corpus where remix share exceeds original share, or where neither Justice nor Soulwax holds a hub position on both sides of the graph, kills the shape law.

rows.claim: The tagger truncates kind words inside the tag itself (TIT2 reads 'NY Excuse - Justice Remi'), so a remix parser without a trailing-'Remi' normalization silently drops the Justice to Soulwax edge instead of flagging anything.
rows.quote: title='NY Excuse - Justice Remi' album='NY Excuse' date=''
rows.steal: One seat, one sitting: add the truncated-suffix normalization (trailing 'Remi' means 'Remix') to any title-suffix parser this estate points at downloaded metadata, and count how many edges it recovers.
rows.falsifier: A parser run with and without the normalization that recovers zero additional edges on this corpus, or a corpus with no truncated kind words, removes the defect.

decision_changed: Closes the curation-direction question for the music-ai folder: batch 2026-08-05 bought the remix network and batch 2026-10-01 backfilled original catalog depth around a fixed 13-artist core, so any later style model for this corpus should train on remix edges and hub degrees, not flat per-artist track lists.
